description: Team ArgentinaSpace — Systems & Quality Lead building AETHER-SIM, a physics-based planetary analog calibration and 1:1 EVA traverse twinning engine. Using NASA POWER, GIBS, and Moon/Mars Trek data, we quantify Earth's gravity/thermal test biases and 4D seasonal validity windows across high-altitude Andean and global analog sites to de-risk Artemis and Mars surface missions.
summary: AETHER-SIM identifies new Earth locations that could serve as analogs for Moon and Mars surface missions. Its Analog Finder scans a region grid, starting with the Puna de Atacama in Salta and Catamarca, Argentina, using live NASA POWER climatology and the Copernicus GLO-90 elevation model. Each cell receives a transparent, heuristic Analog Similarity Index against the chosen Moon or Mars target. Candidates far from any catalogued analog are flagged NEW and sent with one click into a characterization workflow: 2 km traverse comparison against real LOLA/MOLA profiles, a 12-month seasonal window matrix, first-order physics calibration (gravity offload, wheel sinkage, convective bias), and a 3-site campaign plan exported as Markdown or JSON. It is a screening tool, open source, and runs in the browser.
details:
WHAT IT DOES. The challenge asks for new, better-characterized Earth analogs of Moon and Mars sites. AETHER-SIM has two parts. First, the Analog Finder searches a region for candidates: presets cover the Puna de Atacama (NW Argentina, our home region), the Atacama in Chile, the Bolivian Altiplano and Iceland, and it can also scan the current map view. A bundled Puna snapshot loads instantly and "Re-scan live" refreshes it from the data services. Second, a characterization workbench studies any candidate, any of 10 curated sites (including Llullaillaco, Salar de Arizaro and Campo de Piedra Pomez in the Argentine Puna), or any clicked coordinate. Live app: https://gabriel-alejandropereagarcia.github.io/aether-sim/

HOW IT WORKS. For every grid cell the app pulls NASA POWER climatology (temperature, humidity, precipitation, pressure, insolation) and Copernicus GLO-90 elevation via Open-Meteo, and derives local slope. Climatology is corrected to DEM elevation with a standard-atmosphere lapse rate. The Analog Similarity Index combines six factors with transparent, hand-chosen weights that depend on the Moon or Mars target: low pressure, thermal proximity, aridity, diurnal thermal swing, insolation and terrain slope match. Cells are ranked, and any candidate more than 60 km from a catalogued analog is marked NEW.

CHARACTERIZATION. Dual map (NASA GIBS layers beside NASA Moon Trek / Mars Trek); 2 km traverse comparison of a real Copernicus DEM transect against a real planetary profile sampled from the LRO LOLA (118 m/px) or MGS MOLA (463 m/px) global DEM; a 12-month seasonal validity matrix for five test disciplines; a physics calibration lab with first-order models (local gravity offload, Bekker-Wong sinkage, convective heat bias); a 3-site campaign suggestion and Markdown/JSON test protocol export.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT. Widens the search beyond the few famous analog sites with a short, ranked, reproducible list. Every weight and input is shown and every data source is named. Moves from "where" to "how to test there" in one browser tool with no install. Highlights high-altitude terrain close to our own community in Salta and Catamarca.

LIMITATIONS. The index is a heuristic screening tool with hand-chosen weights, not validated by field work. NASA POWER is a coarse reanalysis grid and GLO-90 is about 90 m resolution. On Mars a 2 km line spans only 4-5 MOLA pixels, so slopes are coarse. Radiation, dust charging and vacuum effects need chamber testing. No endorsement by NASA, CONAE, ESA or any agency.

TOOLS. TypeScript, React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Vitest. Runs entirely in the browser, hosted on GitHub Pages. Open source, Apache 2.0.
